title: A city behind barbed wire
episode: The entire city of Ljubljana Slovenia was fenced off in World War II. See how it looks today.
description: In February 1942, Italian forces ringed Ljubljana with barbed wire to cut it off from the partisans in the hills. The fence stayed until May 1945. Its route, about 30 kilometers, is now a footpath, the Path of Remembrance and Comradeship.

title: The first Slovene books
episode: Primoz Trubar: Why Slovenia Celebrates Reformation Day
description: On Primož Trubar, a Protestant preacher who, in exile in Germany, wrote the first books printed in Slovene, a catechism and a primer, in 1550. Reformation Day, October 31, is a public holiday in Slovenia.

title: Napoleon’s Illyria
episode: 3 What Charles Nodier Wrote about the Slovenes | A Story from Napoleonic Illyria
description: From 1809 to 1813, Ljubljana was the capital of Napoleon’s Illyrian Provinces, told here through the French writer Charles Nodier, who edited its newspaper. Plečnik’s column of 1929 is a rare monument to Napoleon outside France.
